prompt: Turn a map of task prerequisites into a legal build order, always choosing the alphabetically smallest task that is ready, and reject any input containing a cycle. Complete the order method in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: This is Kahn's topological sort: count how many prerequisites each task is still waiting on, start with the tasks whose count is zero, and each time you place a task decrement the counts of everything it unlocks. Keeping the ready tasks in a TreeSet makes the alphabetical tie-break free, since first() always hands back the smallest. Two details are easy to miss -- a name that appears only inside a prerequisite list is still a task, and a cycle shows up as the loop stopping with fewer tasks placed than exist, which is when IllegalStateException must be thrown.
hints: First build the full set of task names, including every name that only appears inside a prerequisite list, and a count of outstanding prerequisites for each.
You also need the reverse direction: for each task, which tasks are waiting on it. Build that map at the same time so you can decrement counts when a task is placed.
Keep the ready tasks in a TreeSet and always take first(). When the loop ends, compare the number of tasks placed with the number of tasks that exist -- a shortfall means a cycle.
